title: The Blind Astronomer
text: An old man with no eyes sits on a hill under a sky with no stars you know. He charts the outer dark by touch, on a brass globe pricked with a thousand tiny holes. He hums as he works, and turns the globe toward you before you have said a word.

options.label: Ask him the way through the dark, since he has charted all of it.

outcomes.text: He traces it on the globe with a cracked fingernail, hole by hole, and it is true, every step.

options.label: The sharpest studies his globe of holes, searching for what he has seen.

outcomes.text: One of the holes is new: a star that should not be there, and it is coming closer. They cannot stop looking for it in the sky.

options.label: Take the globe from him. A blind man has no need of stars.

outcomes.text: He weeps without eyes, and the stars overhead begin to go wrong, one by one, as you walk away.
